newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH SPORITELNA CUTS '97 PROFIT FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: CZECH SPORITELNA CUTS '97 PROFIT FORECAST.

text.p: Ceska Sporitelna a.s., the largest Czech savings bank, will see 1997 net profits fall several hundred million crowns below the 2.5 billion originally estimated, the bank's general director said on Tuesday.
Jaroslav Klapal said 1997 profits would be hit by the flooding which has affected large parts of the Czech Republic and the general slowdown in economic growth.

"We do not anticipate that the change in 1997 financial results would be in any way fatally unfavourable. It would be a correction in the hundreds of millions," Sporitelna general director Jaroslav Klapal told a news conference.
A precise, revised, estimate should be available in the second half of September.

The bank had previously set its 1997 net profit estimate according to both international (IAS) and Czech accounting standards at 2.5 billion crowns compared with audited and consolidated IAS 1996 net profits of 2.739 billion crowns.

Klapal said that despite the anticipated fall in profits, Sporitelna would aim to maintain its 1997 dividend payout at the same level -- a gross dividend of 10 crowns on shares with a nominal value of 100 crowns -- as in 1996.
"Our dividend policy is set up such that in years which could be influenced by internal and external problems we are able to maintain a non-declining dividend," Klapal said.
